title: Two Winters
tagline: Guess the year on ten real AI predictions — then watch the same five-stage collapse happen twice
card_blurb: Ten real, sourced predictions with the speaker and the date hidden: guess the year and guess whether it came true. Six confident promises — five have resolved and not one arrived inside the window it named — three confident dismissals that aged worse, and one warning that was right. Then a scrubbable 1950–2026 timeline whose lanes are the five stages of an AI winter — promise, money, limit, naming, withdrawal — firing in order, twice.
description: **Two Winters** — a phone-first, single-file, offline demonstration of the two AI funding collapses of the twentieth century and what they say about this one. Act I is a prediction game: ten real quotations from 1950 to 2024 with the speaker and date hidden, scored on both the year and the outcome, and split at the end into confident promises versus confident dismissals — because the historical record punishes both. Act II is a scrubbable 1950–2026 timeline laid out in five lanes, one per stage of the mechanism, so the repeated sequence is visible rather than asserted, with the two winters as soft-edged bands whose date ranges carry their own disagreement. Act III sets the first winter, the second winter and the present side by side on those same five stages, leaving two cells in the present column openly unanswered. Act IV weighs what rhymes against what is genuinely different. Every claim resolves to a retrievable source and is marked primary or reported; a live self-test proves that in front of the room; and everything researched but not sourceable well enough is listed, with reasons, in a public cut list.
